title: Autonomous LLM Agent Orchestration Engine with ReAct Loop, Deterministic Tool Calling & State Checkpointing
problem: Uncontrolled LLM agents deployed with naive prompt loops suffer from infinite execution cycles, hallucinatory tool parameterization, and total loss of state upon downstream API failures. Relying on opaque framework abstractions obscures tool invocation errors and prevents deterministic workflow resumption. This project builds an autonomous agent orchestration engine in Python. The engine implements a stateful ReAct (Reasoning and Acting) loop, enforces structured tool calling schemas via Pydantic, tracks execution graphs with cycle detection, persists step-by-step workflow state in Redis, and guarantees graceful fallback handling when external tools fail or timeout.

use_cases.title: Automated IT Incident Diagnosis and Remediation
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise DevOps teams need autonomous agents that investigate cloud infrastructure alarms by querying metric APIs, reading server logs, and executing read-only diagnostics.
use_cases.second_sentence: The agent breaks down incident alerts into multi-step investigative plans, executes diagnostic CLI stubs, and synthesizes root-cause summaries without human intervention.

use_cases.title: Automated Customer Support Case Resolution
use_cases.first_sentence: E-commerce customer service platforms require autonomous agents capable of resolving order tracking inquiries, processing authorized refunds, and updating shipping records.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine authenticates customer intents, queries order databases via structured tool calls, verifies business logic guardrails, and returns resolved case statuses.

use_cases.title: Financial Research & SEC Filing Information Extraction
use_cases.first_sentence: Equity research analysts need automated research agents that search financial repositories, calculate accounting ratios, and verify contradictory data across company disclosures.
use_cases.second_sentence: The agent searches document stores, invokes calculator tools for ratio analysis, checks citation validity, and generates structured comparative investment memos.

hard_parts: Preventing infinite reasoning loops and hallucinated circular plans through dynamic depth budgets and cycle detection
Enforcing strict JSON parameter schemas on non-deterministic LLM tool-calling outputs using Pydantic validators
Managing atomic state checkpoints in Redis to enable pause, resume, and rollback capabilities upon tool exceptions
Implementing graceful degradation and alternative tool selection when primary third-party APIs encounter rate limits or timeouts
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase separating ReAct loop controllers, tool plugin registries, and Redis state checkpoint managers
Comprehensive benchmark suite measuring task completion rate, tool call precision, and recovery latency on injected failures
Anti-fake verification script presenting an unseen multi-step problem with an injected broken tool, verifying autonomous fallback to secondary tool

architecture.data_flow: A user request enters the FastAPI execution gateway; the planning controller prompts the LLM to generate an initial Thought and Action; the tool dispatcher validates parameter arguments against the tool's Pydantic schema; if valid, the tool executes within its timeout budget; the Observation result writes to the Redis checkpoint store; if the tool fails, the fallback manager injects error details into the prompt context for replanning; the controller iterates through subsequent Thought-Action-Observation turns until a final answer synthesizes or the step budget exhausts.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Maximum step budget (default 10 iterations) terminating runaway loops; Pydantic argument parsing rejecting malformed tool parameters before execution.

targets.method: Percentage of complex multi-step reasoning goals autonomously completed without human intervention
targets.input: 100 standardized multi-step agent benchmark tasks requiring between 2 and 5 coordinated tool calls
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Python 3.11 with Ollama or local mock LLM provider
targets.minimum_pass: Task completion rate is >= 82.0% across 100 benchmark tasks
targets.target: Task completion rate is >= 93.0% across 100 benchmark tasks
targets.report: Agent benchmark task completion and step efficiency summary report

targets.metric: Tool Parameter Schema Validation Compliance Rate
targets.method: Percentage of generated tool call arguments that conform strictly to defined Pydantic JSON schemas
targets.input: 500 sequential tool call actions generated during multi-step agent execution
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Pydantic v2 runtime validation
targets.minimum_pass: Schema compliance rate is >= 95.0% across 500 generated tool calls
targets.target: Schema compliance rate is >= 99.2% across 500 generated tool calls
targets.report: Tool calling schema compliance and validation rejection log

targets.input: 30 injected tool failure chaos scenarios (HTTP 500, network timeouts, invalid database responses)
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, local Redis 7 container
targets.minimum_pass: Autonomous recovery rate is >= 80.0% across 30 failure scenarios
targets.target: Autonomous recovery rate is >= 93.3% across 30 failure scenarios
targets.report: Chaos tool failure injection and recovery audit log

environment.gpu: None strictly required (compatible with local mock LLM provider or quantized 7B model on CPU)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local mock LLM or Ollama and local Redis)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop (Redis 7 container) and Python 3.11
environment.fallback_path: In-memory dictionary state store if Redis container is unavailable

riskiest_component.name: Runaway Reasoning Cycles on Ambiguous Tool Feedback
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce hard step iteration counters (max 10) and similarity hashing on recent Thought sequences to detect repeating loops.
riskiest_component.fallback: Abort workflow and emit partial execution trace if repeating loop is detected.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an autonomous LLM agent orchestration engine in Python with ReAct planning, Pydantic tool calling, and Redis state checkpointing.
worksheet.q2: Target users: applied AI engineers, automation platform developers, and enterprise backend architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: IT incident diagnosis, automated customer support resolution, and financial SEC filing extraction.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: runaway reasoning cycle detection, strict Pydantic tool parameter enforcement, atomic Redis checkpoint persistence, and dynamic tool failure recovery.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 100 multi-step task definitions, 6 mock tool plugins, and Redis schemas. Synthetic tasks only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: in-memory state dictionary.
